thread:
Anna (PM): Quick sync request — need to lock sequencing for Optimize toolkit: quantization, batching, caching. Customer asks are piling up and we can't ship everything at once. Can we do quick RICE-based proposals + launch criteria in this thread? I sketched an approach below, would love takes.

Raj (Eng): +1. My instinct: batching first (big perf wins for throughput, lower dev risk), then caching (prefix/KV caching quick win), then quantization (higher risk/regression work).

Mike (ML): disagree on order if customer mix is heavy on large LLMs — quantization yields the biggest token cost reduction for 70B+ models. But it needs evals and a lot of CI.

Liz (CS): From field: 3 enterprise customers explicitly asked for deterministic prefix caching and model-pin routes. That suggests caching could be higher priority for renewals.

Anna (PM): All good points. Proposal: we apply a RICE table per feature with some shared assumptions. For speed, here's a simple scoring template (numbers 0-10):
```
Feature | Reach | Impact | Confidence | Effort (months)
Batching | 8 | 6 | 7 | 1.5
Caching  | 6 | 5 | 8 | 1.0
Quant    | 4 | 9 | 5 | 3.0
```
Compute RICE = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort (normalize later). Thoughts?

Raj (Eng): That template works. My quick scores (rough): Batching RICE ~ (8*6*7)/1.5 = 224, Caching ~ (6*5*8)/1 = 240, Quant ~ (4*9*5)/3 = 60. So caching slightly ahead, then batching. But note effort estimates: batching touches runtime kernels + autoscaler, might be 2 months if we account for QA.

Mike (ML): Re: confidence for quantization — set it to 6 if we scope to per-model quant profiles and use existing quant libs. If we add quant-aware kernels and perf tuning confidence drops. Also we should decouple launch criteria: safe-mode (lossless int8 fallback) vs experimental (high memory savings).

Liz (CS): Also weight commercial impact: caching + model pin gives an enterprise sales hook. That increases 'Impact' for caching for sales-led customers.

Anna (PM): OK here's a suggested sequencing that reconciles:
- Phase A (0-3 months): Batching MVP (continuous batching + simple autoscale), Prefix caching alpha (in-memory prefix KV for hosted routes)
- Phase B (3-6 months): Caching GA (durable cache, auth + TTLs), improved batching (kernel-aware routing)
- Phase C (6-12 months): Quantization rollout (model catalog entries, eval harness, canary + rollback)

Launch criteria (draft):
- Batching MVP: end-to-end latency for 99th pct within SLO for target routes, +10% throughput improvement on CI benchmark, rollout with feature flag
- Caching alpha: validated prefix hit-rate >= 20% for test corpora, no correctness regressions on eval prompts, basic telemetry
- Quant GA: automated eval regressions < threshold (quality delta), quantized vs fp32 token cost improvement >= 25% on target models, canary run on <5% traffic with automatic fallback

Raj (Eng): Feels reasonable. A couple of dependency notes:
- Batching MVP needs a short-term kernel selection hook to prefer low-latency kernels for small context lengths. We can get that in 2 sprints if we deprioritize some perf refactors.
- Caching needs a simple metadata API + eviction; ops wants TTLs and a way to opt-out for privacy routes.

Mike (ML): I'll own the quant evaluation plan. Action items: get baseline perf numbers for 4k/8k seqs on 13B/70B, run prototype quant profiles. I can deliver a perf matrix in 2 weeks.

Liz (CS): I'll surface the top 3 customers asking for caching + pinning and collect specific SC/renewal dates.

Anna (PM): Great. Volunteers so far: Raj for batching + infra changes, Mike for quant evals, Liz for customer context. I'll draft a short PRD with the RICE table and the launch criteria above. Anyone wanna edit?

Raj (Eng): I'll add more accurate effort numbers and a dependency map.

Mike (ML): I'll add confidence adjustments and risk mitigation steps for quant.

Liz (CS): I'll add customer quotes and priority dates.

deploy-bot: build #optimize-toolkit-batching started (CI 1248)

Anna (PM): OK team — let's aim to have the PRD draft by EOD Friday. Quick poll: are we all aligned on the sequencing (Batching + Cache -> Quant)? Reply with :thumbsup: or :thumbsdown:.

Raj (Eng): :thumbsup:
Mike (ML): :thumbsup: (with caveat on enterprise needs)
Liz (CS): :thumbsup:
Anna (PM): :thumbsup: Thanks — I'll post the PRD link in this thread when ready.
